subject: Electrical Engineering
title: VFDs: Variable Frequency Drives
description: One-minute skill: VFDs: Variable Frequency Drives.

hook.text: AC motors are designed for one speed. A VFD lets you choose any speed you want.

buildup.text: The VFD converts AC to DC, then synthesizes new AC at any desired frequency.

discovery.text: Lower frequency means slower rotation. Higher frequency means faster. Smooth, stepless control.

twist.text: VFDs save 20-50% energy in pumps and fans by matching motor speed to actual demand.

climax.text: Elevators, HVAC systems, and conveyor belts all use VFDs for efficient speed control.

punchline.text: Control frequency, control speed — VFDs freed motors from one pace.

quiz.question: How does a VFD control motor speed?
options: By varying the voltage while keeping frequency constant
By converting AC to DC, then creating new AC at a desired frequency
By switching the motor between series and parallel winding configurations
